name: Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock)
why: A flat square of rock 604 m straight above the Lysefjord, reached by a stone-stepped path over bare granite slabs and small lakes.
book: Free: the Norwegian right to roam (allemannsretten). Paid parking at the trailhead. Bus from Stavanger to Preikestolen Fjellstue in summer (about 1 h). Go early or late: by noon hundreds walk it.
water: No water on the way: carry 1.5 litres. Cafe at the Fjellstue.
dangers: Unfenced 604 m drop: keep away from the edge, never sit on it in wind.
Weather turns fast: fog, rain and wind even in July. Check yr.no and turn back in fog.
Ice on the slabs from November to April: go with a guide and spikes.
turnaround: If fog hides the next cairn, go back.
